title: Global Climate Classification — Köppen–Trewartha
text:
Introduction
This project analyzes changes in global climate classification across three climate intervals, beginning with the 1961–1990 WMO Climatological Reference Period and extending through the 2021–2025 Recent Climate Interval, using ERA5 temperature and precipitation data from the Copernicus Climate Data Store.
The analysis applies the Köppen–Trewartha climate classification system consistently to each interval, compares the resulting climate classifications, quantifies transitions among climate groups and types, and maps where those transitions occur.

title: Global Climate Classification — Köppen–Trewartha
text:
Climate Periods
The project uses three non-overlapping analysis periods and one consistent terminology throughout the workflow:

WMO Climatological Reference Period (1961–1990) — the 1961–1990 period retained by WMO as a standard reference period for long-term climate-change assessment.
WMO Climatological Standard Normals (1991–2020) — the current WMO 30-year climatological standard normal.
Recent Climate Interval (2021–2025) — a project-defined recent five-year interval used to identify emerging climate signals. It is not a WMO climatological normal.

For compact tables or figures, the project uses the abbreviations REF, CSN, and RCI. These labels are intended to be used consistently in this project and in the companion Global Temperature Change Analysis project.

title: Global Climate Classification — Köppen–Trewartha
text:
Köppen–Trewartha Climate Classification
The Köppen–Trewartha climate classification used in this project contains six broad climate groups and thirteen climate types:

Group A — Tropical

Ar — Tropical Rainforest
Aw — Tropical Savanna

Group B — Dry

BW — Desert (Arid)
BS — Steppe (Semiarid)

Group C — Subtropical

Cs — Mediterranean (dry summer)
Cw — Subtropical (dry winter)
Cf — Subtropical (no dry season)

Group D — Temperate

Do — Temperate (Oceanic)
Dc — Temperate (Continental)

Group E — Boreal

Eo — Boreal (Oceanic)
Ec — Boreal (Continental)

Group F — Polar

Ft — Tundra
Fi — Ice Cap

title: Global Climate Classification — Köppen–Trewartha
text: Workflow

title: Global Climate Classification — Köppen–Trewartha
text:
Workflow
The project uses monthly ERA5 temperature and precipitation climatologies prepared by the companion ERA5-DATA project. That project handles ERA5 acquisition and transformation, producing reusable datasets for the REF, CSN, and RCI climate intervals.
The climate-classification analysis is organized into four sequential stages:

Determinant Calculation
Read the transformed ERA5 climatologies from the shared ERA5-DATA project and calculate the temperature, precipitation, and aridity determinants required by the Köppen–Trewartha classification system.
Climate Classification
Apply the same Köppen–Trewartha classification rules to each grid cell for the REF, CSN, and RCI climate intervals; create the classification reference tables and coastline layer; and summarize the resulting climate groups and types.
Transition Analysis
Quantify climate-group and climate-type transitions for REF → CSN, CSN → RCI, and REF → RCI; examine transition matrices; and calculate gains, losses, and net classification changes.
Transition Mapping
Map the geographic distribution of climate-classification changes, including broad spatial patterns, expansion of dry and desert classifications, retreat of polar classifications, and the long-term REF → RCI transition pattern.

The ERA5-DATA and Global Climate Classification — Köppen–Trewartha projects are maintained as sibling directories under ~/Projects/. Shared climate datasets remain in ERA5-DATA, while classification determinants, classifications, transition datasets, and mapping outputs belong to this analysis project.

title: Global Climate Classification — Köppen–Trewartha
text:
Data
This analysis uses ERA5 reanalysis data produced by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) and distributed through the Copernicus Climate Data Store.
The companion ERA5-DATA project acquires and transforms the source data into reusable monthly climatologies for the three analysis intervals (REF, CSN, and RCI).
The shared datasets contain:

Monthly 2 m air temperature
Monthly total precipitation

These transformed datasets are read from the sibling project at ../era5-data/data/transformed/.
The climate-classification project maintains its own derived analytical datasets and static reference data, including:

Köppen–Trewartha climate-group definitions and colors
Köppen–Trewartha climate-type definitions and colors
Natural Earth global coastline data

The ERA5 land-sea mask is an additional source dataset used in the broader data-preparation workflow.

title: Global Climate Classification — Köppen–Trewartha
text:
Software
Programming Language: R
Development Environment: Positron
Document Creation: Quarto
Major R packages used in the climate-classification analysis include:

arrow – Parquet data import and export
fs – File and directory operations
gt – Summary tables
patchwork – Plot layouts
rnaturalearth – Natural Earth geographic data
sf – Spatial data processing and mapping
terra – Raster processing and spatial analysis
tidyverse – Data manipulation and visualization
viridisLite – Climate-period color palettes

The project uses renv for reproducible R package management. Package versions are recorded in renv.lock.
ERA5 acquisition and transformation are handled separately by the companion ERA5-DATA project.

title: Determinant Calculation
text:
Determinants
The determinant calculations are applied independently to each climate interval.

Temperature

TAVG — annual average temperature (°C)
TMAX — monthly maximum temperature (°C)
TMIN — monthly minimum temperature (°C)
TG10 — number of months with average temperature ≥ 10 °C



Precipitation

PTOT — annual total precipitation (mm)
PWNT — winter total precipitation (mm)
PSMR — summer total precipitation (mm)
PMIN — monthly minimum precipitation (mm)
PL60 — number of months with total precipitation < 60 mm



Aridity

ATHR — aridity threshold (cm)

The aridity threshold is calculated as:
R = 2.3T − 0.64Pw + 41
where R is the aridity threshold in centimetres, T is average annual air temperature in °C, and Pw is the percentage of annual precipitation occurring in winter.
Reference: https://www.int-res.com/articles/cr_oa/c059p001.pdf


Show code
t_determinants <- c(
  "TAVG",
  "TMAX",
  "TMIN",
  "TG10"
)

p_determinants <- c(
  "PTOT",
  "PWNT",
  "PSMR",
  "PMIN",
  "PL60"
)

a_determinants <- "ATHR"

aridity_variables <- c(
  "wpct",
  "trm1",
  "trm2",
  "trm3"
)

determinants <- c(
  t_determinants,
  p_determinants,
  aridity_variables,
  a_determinants
)

determinant_metadata <- tribble(
  ~Determinant, ~Description,                                      ~Role,                   ~Group,

  "TMAX",       "Monthly Maximum Temperature (°C)",                "Primary Determinant",  "Temperature",
  "TMIN",       "Monthly Minimum Temperature (°C)",                "Primary Determinant",  "Temperature",
  "TG10",       "Months with Average Temperature ≥ 10°C",          "Derived Determinant",  "Temperature",
  "PTOT",       "Annual Total Precipitation (mm)",                 "Primary Determinant",  "Precipitation",
  "PWNT",       "Winter Total Precipitation (mm)",                 "Primary Determinant",  "Precipitation",
  "PSMR",       "Summer Total Precipitation (mm)",                 "Primary Determinant",  "Precipitation",
  "PMIN",       "Monthly Minimum Precipitation (mm)",              "Primary Determinant",  "Precipitation",
  "PL60",       "Months with Total Precipitation < 60 mm",         "Derived Determinant",  "Precipitation",
  "wpct",       "Winter % of Total Precipitation (%)",             "Intermediate Metric",  "Aridity",
  "trm1",       "Term 1: TAVG × 2.3",                              "Formula Term",          "Aridity",
  "trm2",       "Term 2: Winter Precipitation % × 0.64",           "Formula Term",          "Aridity",
  "trm3",       "Term 3: Constant 41",                             "Formula Term",          "Aridity",

title: Climate Classification
text:
Classification Method
Objective: Assign Köppen–Trewartha climate classifications to each ERA5 grid cell for the REF, CSN, and RCI climate intervals. This notebook applies a common classification sequence to the determinant dataset created in the previous step, saves a unified classification dataset for transition analysis, and summarizes the geographic distribution of climate groups and types across the three intervals.
The Köppen–Trewartha classification is assigned sequentially so that each grid cell receives exactly one climate group and type.
The classification thresholds below are preserved from the original GCCCA workflow.

title: Climate Classification
text:
Group F — Polar: classified from TMAX.
Group B — Dry: classified from ATHR and PTOT.
Group A — Tropical: classified from TMIN and PL60.
Group C — Subtropical: classified from TG10, PTOT, PWNT, PSMR, and PMIN.
Group D — Temperate: classified from TG10 and TMIN.
Group E — Boreal: classified from TG10 and TMIN.

Global Maps
The maps show the geographic distribution of Köppen–Trewartha climate types for each climate interval using a common classification palette. The broad spatial patterns are intentionally similar because most grid cells retain the same climate classification across the three intervals. These maps provide a geographic check of the classification results; changes between intervals are examined directly in the transition-analysis stage.

  classification_results,
  "reference_period"
)

map_csn <- fn_build_global_map(
  classification_results,
  "standard_normal"
)

  classification_results,
  "recent_interval"
)

title: Transition Analysis
text:
Transition Comparisons
Objective: Analyze changes in Köppen–Trewartha climate classifications among the REF, CSN, and RCI climate intervals. This notebook quantifies how much global land area changes climate group or type, identifies the most important transitions, summarizes net gains and losses by classification, and saves a unified transition dataset for geographic mapping in the final stage of the workflow.
Three pairwise comparisons are used to separate historical, recent, and long-term classification change:
Transition calculations use land-area weighting based on the ERA5 grid-cell area multiplied by the fractional land-sea mask.

title: Transition Analysis
text:
REF → CSN — change from the 1961–1990 WMO Climatological Reference Period to the 1991–2020 WMO Climatological Standard Normals.
CSN → RCI — change from the 1991–2020 standard normal to the 2021–2025 Recent Climate Interval.
REF → RCI — the full contrast between the reference period and the recent interval.

change_overview |>
  select(
    comparison_label,
    group_changed_pct,
    type_changed_pct
  ) |>

    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)

  labs(
    title = "Land Area with Changed KTC Classification",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Global Land Area %",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()

title: Transition Mapping
text:
Initialization
Objective: Map the geographic distribution of Köppen–Trewartha climate-classification transitions among the REF, CSN, and RCI climate intervals. This notebook shows where climate types changed, distinguishes within-group type changes from broader climate-group changes, examines the expansion of dry and desert climate classifications and the retreat of polar classifications, and provides a long-term spatial summary of change from REF to RCI.
The transition-analysis notebook quantified how much land changed classification and identified the most important transitions. This final stage adds the geographic dimension: where did those changes occur?

Overall Spatial Pattern of Change
These maps show only grid cells whose KTC type changed. Cells that remained within the same broad climate group are distinguished from cells that crossed a climate-group boundary. Unchanged land is omitted so that the spatial pattern of change is not overwhelmed by the much larger stable classification area.

title: Transition Mapping
section: Expansion of Dry and Desert Climate Classifications
text:
Expansion of Dry and Desert Climate Classifications
The following maps focus on long-term REF → RCI transitions into increasingly dry Köppen–Trewartha classifications. These maps describe climate-classification change, not land degradation or desertification.

Expansion into Group B — Dry
This map shows grid cells that were not classified as Group B during REF but are classified as Group B during RCI. Changed cells are colored by their origin climate group, showing both where dry climates expanded and which broad climate classifications they replaced.


Show code
fn_build_themed_transition_map(
  transitions_df = transition_results,
  comparison_id = "ref_rci",
  filter_expression =
    from_grp != "B" &
    to_grp == "B",
  color_variable = "from_grp",
  color_levels = group_levels,
  palette = group_palette,
  title = "Expansion into KTC Group B — Dry",
  subtitle = "new Group B grid cells colored by origin climate group",
  legend_title = "Origin Group"
)











Transition into Type BW — Desert
This map isolates the more specific transition into the KTC BW — Desert (Arid) climate type. Changed cells are colored by their origin climate type, allowing the locations and prior classifications of newly classified desert climates to be examined directly.


Show code
fn_build_themed_transition_map(
  transitions_df = transition_results,
  comparison_id = "ref_rci",
  filter_expression =
    from_ktc != "BW" &
    to_ktc == "BW",
  color_variable = "from_ktc",
  color_levels = type_levels,
  palette = type_palette,
  title = "Transition into KTC Type BW — Desert",
  subtitle = "new BW grid cells colored by origin climate type",
  legend_title = "Origin Type"
)

title: Transition Mapping
text:
Retreat of Polar Climate Classifications
This map shows grid cells classified as Group F — Polar during REF that are assigned to a different climate group during RCI. Changed cells are colored by their destination climate group, showing where polar classifications retreated and which broad climates replaced them.


Show code
fn_build_themed_transition_map(
  transitions_df = transition_results,
  comparison_id = "ref_rci",
  filter_expression =
    from_grp == "F" &
    to_grp != "F",
  color_variable = "to_grp",
  color_levels = group_levels,
  palette = group_palette,
  title = "Retreat of KTC Group F — Polar",
  subtitle = "former Group F grid cells colored by destination climate group",
  legend_title = "Destination Group"
)

title: Transition Mapping
text:
Long-Term Spatial Summary
The final map emphasizes the broadest project comparison, REF → RCI. It shows only grid cells that changed KTC climate group, with each changed cell colored by its destination group. Stable land is omitted so that the spatial structure of long-term classification change remains visible.


Show code
fn_build_long_term_group_map(
  transition_results
)
